meta.title: The potential adverse effects of hypodermic glucagon-like peptide -1 receptor agonist on patients with type 2 diabetes: A population-based study.
meta.abstract:
Background

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), a class of injectable antidiabetic drugs, have shown significant efficacies in improving glycemic and weight control in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the long-term safety of GLP-1 RAs remains insufficiently studied. This study aimed to provide real-world evidence on potential adverse outcomes associated with GLP-1 RAs use in T2D patients without major chronic diseases including impaired cardiac or renal function.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 7746 T2D patients on GLP-1 RAs in Shenzhen, China. They were compared with 124 371 metformin-only users and 36 146 insulin-only users, forming two therapy control groups. GLP-1 RAs users were also further 1:2 paired with the control groups. Competing risk survival analyses were conducted to assess the incidence risks, presenting subdistributional hazard ratios (sHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for various adverse outcomes associated with GLP-1 RAs use.

Results

Compared with metformin-only users, GLP-1 RAs use was associated with increased risks of various adverse outcomes (sHRs with 95% CIs), including pancreatitis (2.01, 1.24-3.24), acute nephritis (3.20, 2.17-4.70), kidney failure (3.73, 2.74-5.08), thyroid cancer (2.25, 1.23-4.10), and thyroid dysfunction (1.27, 1.00-1.63), respectively; Similar results were also found when compared with insulin-only users. Importantly, long-term (≥12 months) GLP-1 RAs use may further elevate the incidence risks of pancreatitis, acute nephritis, thyroid cancer, and thyroid dysfunction.

Conclusion

Compared with traditional T2D treatments, GLP-1 RAs use may be associated with increased risks of various adverse outcomes in a Chinese population. Cautions were strongly warranted in the use of GLP-1 RAs. Further validation is crucial across diverse populations.

domains.name: Confounding
domains.direction_justification: GLP-1 RA users at baseline had markedly higher rates of obesity (BMI 30.0-39.9 kg/m2: 13.21% in GLP-1 RAs vs 4.87% in metformin and 3.04% in insulin) and higher citizen health insurance coverage (75.60% vs 54.96% in metformin), predisposing them to both higher baseline risk of comorbidities and increased clinical surveillance.

findings.title: Severe unmeasured and residual confounding by indication and disease severity
findings.mechanism: Type 2 diabetes severity, duration, and key clinical prognostic variables could not be controlled because key biomarkers had massive missingness (HbA1c was missing in 90.52% to 91.79% of patients; fasting plasma glucose missing in 24.13% to 32.95%). Matching on 'unspecified' missing categories does not balance actual underlying clinical severity.
evidence: Missing rate for HbA1c was 91.27% overall (Table 1 footnote) and 90.52% in GLP-1 RA, 91.79% in insulin, 90.45% in metformin (Table 3S footnote).
Missing rate for FPG was 33.22% overall and 32.95% in GLP-1 RAs, 32.66% in insulin, 24.13% in metformin.

domains.name: Selection of participants into the study
domains.direction_justification: Out of 985,278 initial diabetes outpatients, 362,035 were excluded for missing prescription data, 177,381 for missing IDs, and 55,321 for prevalent conditions, leaving a highly selected subset (380,370 eligible) without validation of selection mechanisms.

findings.title: Massive cohort attrition from database exclusion criteria
findings.mechanism: Excluding over 60% of the initial outpatient registry due to missing identifiers and missing prescription data can induce selection bias if data capture is related to treatment regimen or outcome development.
evidence: Total screened: 985,278; excluded for missing ID: 177,381; excluded for missing prescription data: 362,035 (Figure 1).

domains.name: Post-exposure interventions
domains.direction_justification: Patients could receive other antidiabetic medications for up to 6 months without being excluded, and differential co-treatments across arms were not tracked over time.

findings.title: Unaccounted concomitant medications
findings.mechanism: Permitting up to 6 months of concomitant non-assigned antidiabetic prescriptions without time-varying adjustment may distort effect estimates.
evidence: Accumulative prescription period of any other antidiabetic medication <6 months allowed in exposure and control groups.

domains.name: Missing data
domains.direction_justification: PSM matched on missing indicator categories ('Unspecified' BMI: 33.81% GLP-1 vs 36.08% Insulin; 'Unspecified' Age: 20.53% vs 21.93%; 'Unspecified' Education: 33.62% vs 35.89%), leaving substantial true baseline imbalance unaddressed.

findings.title: Extensive missingness in key confounders handled via missing indicator category
findings.mechanism: Matching on 'Unspecified' as a discrete category creates pseudo-balance in missingness patterns rather than actual clinical characteristics, masking severe underlying confounding.
evidence: In PSM cohort (Table 1): Age unspecified in 20.53% (GLP-1) vs 21.93% (Insulin); Education unspecified in 33.62% vs 35.89%; BMI unspecified in 33.81% vs 36.08%; HbA1c missing rate 91.27%.

domains.name: Measurement of the outcome
domains.direction_justification: Patients initiated on novel, expensive injectable therapies (GLP-1 RAs with 75.60% citizen insurance vs 54.96% in metformin) undergo more frequent outpatient contact and biochemical surveillance, increasing detection of subclinical or routine diagnostic codes (e.g., acute nephritis, thyroid nodules/dysfunction, cysts).

findings.title: Surveillance bias and unadjudicated electronic health record diagnostic coding
findings.mechanism: Outcomes were extracted using ICD-10 codes combined with regular expression text matching from routine electronic records without clinical adjudication or standardized monitoring intervals.
evidence: Outcomes identified via ICD-10 and regular expression matching (Table 2S) across unadjudicated outpatient and inpatient records.
Elevated hazard ratios observed across widely disparate, non-specific outcomes including acne (sHR 5.32, 95% CI 2.21-12.81) and leukemia (sHR 15.09, 95% CI 4.65-48.98).

domains.name: Selection of the reported result
domains.direction_justification: Multiple outcomes and multiple sub-analyses were conducted across multiple control groups without an explicit pre-registered analysis plan.

findings.title: Multiple testing across exploratory endpoints
findings.mechanism: Analyses spanned 19 distinct adverse outcome categories across multiple subgroups and exposure durations without family-wise error rate control.
evidence: 19 clinical conditions assessed across two distinct control populations and four individual drug subgroups.

overall.summary: The study has very high risk of bias stemming primarily from critical missing data in essential confounders (HbA1c missing in >90% of participants, BMI/education missing in >30%), where propensity score matching matched on 'unspecified' missing categories rather than actual values. Furthermore, substantial confounding by indication, selection bias from excluding over 500,000 registry patients, and surveillance/detection bias for patients on novel injectable therapies undermine the causal validity of the reported associations.

unresolvable_without_more_data: Complete baseline laboratory data (actual HbA1c, fasting glucose, renal function tests eGFR/uACR) for the >90% missing cohort.
Raw event counts and person-time per treatment arm for each specific adverse event.
Information on surveillance frequency and outpatient visit counts across exposure groups to quantify detection bias.

baseline_comparability.summary: Baseline differences show GLP-1 RA users were younger but markedly more obese and had higher health insurance coverage than comparator cohorts.
